name: index_momentum_5s
author: adapted from AI_Quant
thesis: This strategy trades based on index momentum. It enters long (short) when the Nifty50's 5-minute return is strongly positive (negative), exploiting the tendency of individual stocks to follow overall market moves (market beta). This inefficiency exists because index movements (often driven by institutional flows or macro announcements) are not always fully anticipated by individual stock prices. It persists due to market friction and the broad-based nature of moves.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.
weaknesses: Only works if stock is highly correlated with index; idiosyncratic moves break the setup
Small edge due to broad-based nature, may not overcome costs
Index returns may already price in general market sentiment
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
